reason: The fruit is described as 1-locular with 'septum absent'. Septum (PO:0000030) present, negated, says exactly that.
Inner phyllaries are involucral bracts, and the 'inner' slot (FLOPO:0991378) restricts the bearer correctly. 'Narrowly elliptic' maps to elliptic and only loses the degree word, which is not false.

target: tuberous root (PO_0025523), with amount 2 and oblong shape
fix: 'Rootstock of N <shape> tubers' describes the tubers: their number and shape. It does not merely assert that a root is present. In Aconitum these are root tubers.
reason: The statement gives the number (two) and shape (oblong) of the tubers that make up the rootstock. 'Root present' is trivially true but is not what the flora says.

The fruits are said to be 'not sulcate', and the annotation negates sulcate (FLOPO:0991061) on the fruit. The attribute slot reads texture, while sulcate sits under PATO:0001948 furrowed. That is a slot-label detail and does not change the meaning.
In translated Kew Latin, 'graceful' renders gracilis, meaning slender. So slender inflorescences matches the source.
'Stamens 18–20, shorter than petals' is annotated as stamen, decreased length, compared to petal.
'Leaves numerous' is annotated as leaf present with count word 'many', which is right.
1–5 teeth on each side of the leaflet margin is annotated as lamina tooth, amount 1–5, inside the leaflet, with position 'each side'.

target: length at most 12 cm (upper bound only)
fix: 'to N' or 'up to N' gives a maximum. It should be recorded as an open range (min unknown, max N), not as the exact value N–N.

fix: The container would be more precise as the verticillaster (the partial inflorescence), not the whole raceme. 'N-flowered' after a partial-inflorescence noun counts flowers per partial unit.
reason: The verticillasters are 2–16-flowered. Generic inflorescence (PO_0009049) as the container still covers the verticillaster, so the statement is not false.
0.4–4 dm converts correctly to 4–40 cm stem length.

fix: 'Indistinctly contracted' (also 'gradually' or 'slightly' contracted) means a barely marked, gradual narrowing. The degree word reverses the sense of FLOPO:0991316 'abruptly narrowed', which should apply only to unmodified 'contracted' or 'abruptly or suddenly contracted'.
reason: An oblanceolate leaf 'indistinctly contracted toward base' narrows gradually. Recording it as abruptly narrowed says the opposite.
The calyx lobes taper at the apex. Sepal apex, tapered is a fair reading of the lobes of a joined calyx.
'Cymes 1–5 per node' is annotated as cyme amount 1–5 with position 'per node'.
The second dimension in 'Fruit 2–4 × 1.5–2.5 mm' is the width, 1.5–2.5 mm.

'Seed dark reddish-brown' maps directly to dark reddish brown (FLOPO:0988070).

fix: The first alternative, 'rhombic', is not captured. The range is 'rhombic to narrowly ovate to lanceolate'; a chain of three values should give two continuum links.
reason: Receptacular bracts are bracts, and the narrowly ovate-to-lanceolate continuum is in the text. Leaving out 'rhombic' does not make the statement false.

The petals are 'glabrous within', i.e. on the inner (adaxial) side. This follows the established pattern of substituting the adaxial epidermis as the bearer.

fix: The third alternative, 'brownish', is not captured. 'A to B or C' should keep C as an alternative.
reason: The spikelets are whitish to greenish, a colour continuum. Reading the '-ish' endings as 'approximately' is acceptable, and leaving out 'brownish' is not false.

fix: '<side> side <shape>' after 'base asymmetrical' describes one side of the pinna base, not the whole pinna. Also, a hyphenated shape compound such as 'attenuate-cuneate' is a single blended shape (attenuately cuneate), not a continuum from one value to the other.
reason: The whole pinna is quadrangular-trapeziform. Only the basiscopic side of its base is attenuate-cuneate, so giving the whole pinna that shape is false.
'Basal leaves rosulate' is annotated as leaf rosulate with the basal slot (FLOPO:0991002).

fix: The height (up to 3.5 m) could also be captured.
reason: The plant varies from a suffrutex to a large shrub. A shrubby (frutescent) habit is one of the stated forms.

target: lobe of the basal pinna; 'basal' qualifies the pinna (the whole), not the lobe
fix: Context words that name the parent ('basal pinnae ... lobes ...') should fill the whole slot. They should not become a position quality of the lobe, and they should not be taken from the later 'basal pairs nearly free'.
reason: 'Acuminate' is said of all the lobes of the pinna being described. Marking the lobes themselves as basal claims only the basal lobes are acuminate.
The inflorescence branches are reddish. Red with 'approximately' follows the colour crosswalk (reddish is related to red).
'Whitish pink' is one alternative corolla colour and falls within pink (ISCC-NBS level 2).
'Without lenticels' on the branches is annotated as lenticel present, negated.
In Euphorbia, ray-leaves are bracts. 'Rounded at the apex' maps to obtuse (synonym roundish) on the bract apex.
